latest_release.body:
## What's Changed
* Clarify interface in-discard counter by @dplore in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1562
* Create initial gemini code assist styleguide by @dplore in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1556
* Add @navaneethyv as a default code owner by @dplore in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1565
* Add support for connection point status by @arun-arista in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1532
* Add support for IPv6 RA reachable-time and router-preference by @vishak-mut in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1543
* Add PACKAGED_TRANSCEIVER component type by @mrevang in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1539
* Add ospf administrative distance by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1544
* Refactor contributions guide for improved readability by @bradlitterell in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1509
* Add ospf auto cost reference bandwidth by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1545
* Add MACSec interface status and MKA security-policy leaf by @dplore in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1430
* Add ospf maximum ecmp paths by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1546
* Add ospf nsr by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1547
* Add ospf send default route by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1548
* Add ospf three stage spf lsa timers by @ky-teramae in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1549
* Add in-profile-dscp and out-profile-dscp to GRE and UDP encap-headers by @nokia1adam in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1561
* Add per-interface ICMPv6 and IPv6 ND message counters by @vishak-mut in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1563
* Add support for static endpoint by @arun-arista in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1530
* Add `ingress-sa-failure` counter to IPsec connection counters by @romeyod in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1574
* Add DSCP leaf to GRE encapsulation config by @dongping-zhu in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1510
* Local-as refactoring and extension by @rszarecki in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1508
* Add 1600G and 3200G ZR/ZR+ PMD and tributary protocol identities by @ahsaanyousaf in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1585
* openconfig macsec sak-rekey-on-live-peer-loss description update by @ishwarbnaik in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1456

## New Contributors
* @arun-arista made their first contribution in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1532
* @vishak-mut made their first contribution in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1543
* @bradlitterell made their first contribution in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1509
* @dongping-zhu made their first contribution in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1510
* @ahsaanyousaf made their first contribution in https://github.com/openconfig/public/pull/1585

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/openconfig/public/compare/v5.10.0...v5.11.0

# OpenConfig

[**OpenConfig**](http://www.openconfig.net) is a collaborative effort by network
operators to develop programmatic interfaces and tools for managing networks in
a dynamic, vendor-neutral way.  OpenConfig’s initial focus is on compiling a
consistent set of vendor-neutral data models (written in
[YANG](http://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc6020/)) based on actual operational
needs from use cases and requirements from multiple network operators.

## Contributing to OpenConfig

This repository is primarily for publishing the models, documents, and other
material developed by the OpenConfig operators group.

For information about how to contribute to OpenConfig models, please
see [External Submissions to OpenConfig](doc/contributions-guide.md).

Feedback and suggestions to improve OpenConfig models is welcomed on the
[public mailing list](https://groups.google.com/forum/?hl=en#!forum/netopenconfig),
or by opening a GitHub [issue](https://github.com/openconfig/public/issues).

## Joining OpenConfig

Please see the [OpenConfig web site](http://www.openconfig.net) for information
for operators wishing to join OpenConfig, in particular the
[FAQ for operators](https://openconfig.net/docs/faqs/operator_faq/).
